tool_input.description: Check whether fldigi CWspeed follows receive tracking

result:
Unit 463 is complete (task 4 of 4, nothing dropped), but it did not advance: both fldigi front-end forms were refused under R78 and reverted, so 9.4 stays open. Nothing under `src` changed, and every recording reads exactly as before.

| form | real (MET-CER-SURE / MET-INVENTED / coverage / MET-WBE) | synthetic | adjudicated | recordings worse (of 35) | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | 33/436, 33, 403, 37 | 14/173, 14, 159, 44 | 13 of 13 | ΓÇö | ΓÇö |
| (A1) half-dit integrator at the read's speed | 13/51, 13, 38/453, 89 | 1/85, 1, 84, 60 | 7 of 13 | 26 | refused |
| (A2) fldigi's AGC dividing our level | 39/442, 39, 403, 37 | 33/182, 33, 149, 46 | 13 of 13 | 11 | refused |

- **(A1)** made the decoder print almost nothing: 38 right letters on the real recordings instead of 403. The trace suggests why. Our noise estimate assumes the envelope is raw noise from one pair of channels, and fldigi's half-dit averaging breaks that assumption. So every mark looks close to noise and most get refused.
- **(A2)** came closer. It kept all 13 checked readings, but printed 6 more wrong letters on the real recordings and 19 more on the generated ones, and made 11 recordings worse.
- **Silence** held under both forms: nothing was printed on either empty band.
- **What this leaves:** every fldigi mechanism 9.3 named, (A) to (E), has now been refused. The plan's rule R86 still blocks steps 2 to 8 until 9.4 has a kept change. The report states this as a fact and proposes nothing; the next arbiter decides what comes next.
- **Exit round:** every figure matches entry. The port and the eleven transmit files are unchanged, and both decoders' texts are identical to task 0's. `TheSpeedFollowsTheSendersMarkPairsTests` still fails at 28 of 31, as unit 459 left it.

Things that differed from the instruction:
- There is no `.run-unit\watched.rc`.
- I logged `outcome-read`'s step-title mismatch as the instruction describes it, without running the tool.
- On the first entry run the app line lost 2 tests to Avalonia's dispatcher loop; the one allowed rerun passed 278 of 278.
- In the commit table, the middle commits' test lines weren't re-run at each commit. They rest on unchanged `src` between two green measurements, and the table says so.

I also found that the parity harness's "port unchanged" check can fail when only our decoder changes: under (A1) one port line disappeared from the save even though the port wasn't touched. That's item 4 in section 4.

Commits, all pushed to `origin/main`: `41f445ef`, `06bcd261`, `90713038`, `17e1ae57`, `99c90b69`. `PROJECT_STATUS.md` is set to COMPLETED, and `output.md` passes the project's validator.
